text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- NATO Secretary-General Javier, on first visit to Finland at end-month, expected to elaborate on implications of Nato's partnership for peace, to which Finland is favourably disposed.
- Tampere-based daily Aamulehti wants more youthful journalists. Plans to negotiate with all journalists aged 53 years to either go part-time or quit.
- Foreign affairs committee of the Lutheran Church wants Finland to follow more humanitarian and wide-reaching refugee policy. Says current policy is full of pitfalls.
- Farmers in north Finland sharply oppose plans to scale down milk production quotas.
- Forestry groups Enso and UPM-Kymmene plan to stop paying into joint worker-controlled bonus funds, change to system of directly paying staff if results are good.
- Imatra Voima's market value would be higher than Neste's, preliminary estimates show. IVO is valued at up 25 billion markka while Neste's market value is over nine billion markka.
- Downturn expected in industrial investment in 1998. Not much growth will be realised in the construction sector either which would be engine of new investments.

- Former President of the EU Commission Jacques Delors said EMU will not be a success if it only remains within central banks. Balance must be found for economic and monetary union in politics as well as in economics.
- Finland's administrative structure handling EU affairs must be put in better shape, says State Audit Office.
- Over one-quarter of the registered Finnish voters are pensioners but their votes are widely dispersed and do not necessarily go to pensioners' party.
- Finland's Post Office expects preliminary voting in EU and municipal elections to exceed one million record borderline in spite of reduction in voting time from two weeks to one.
